answers.answer: Starting Player cards are 4 each for 2 players, 3 each for 3 players, and 2 each for 4 players. Remove and set aside Epidemic cards before dealing; shuffle the remaining City and Event cards for the deal. Pawns start in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 5–6: matching pawns in Atlanta; remove Epidemic cards and deal from the remaining Player cards.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2. Reveal 3 cities and put 3 matching cubes on each; reveal 3 more and put 2 on each; reveal 3 more and put 1 on each. Put all 9 revealed Infection cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: leftmost ‘2’; 3/2/1 cubes for each successive group; revealed cards to discard pile and remaining cards form deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemic cards for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemic cards from the game. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible, shuffle one Epidemic into each pile, then stack the piles with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: difficulty counts, unused Epidemics removed, piles ‘equal in number’ and ‘as equal in size as possible,’ then stacked smaller piles on bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions, repeating actions if desired or stopping early. Action-cost cards go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve Epidemics first and discard or play Events until within the hand limit; then Infect Cities. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: up to 4 actions, may repeat/stop, action discards to Player Discard Pile; phases are actions, draw, infect; turn passes left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves along a white line to a connected city, with no card cost. Direct Flight discards the destination city's card. Charter Flight discards the card matching the city you are in and moves to any city. Shuttle Flight moves from a city with a research station to any other city with a research station. White lines going off one board edge wrap to the other edge (example: Sydney and Los Angeles).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table and Special Rules & Edge Cases: white lines going off an edge wrap to the other edge.

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it there. If all 6 are built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set the extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Build a Research Station action and Research station limit / ‘If more than 6 stations supplied’ edge cases.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes 1 cube of one chosen color from the city, even if that disease is cured; for a cured color, the action instead removes all cubes of that color from the city. Each different color needs its own action. Removed cubes return to the cube supply. The summary does not give an additional procedure for clearing other colors beyond treating each color with a separate action.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: remove 1 cube of a chosen color, or all cubes of that color if cured; separate action per different color; cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. The station city need not match the disease color. Existing cubes remain, and the disease can still receive cubes until eradicated. If no cubes of that color are on the board when the cure is discovered, immediately eradicate it and flip its marker.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: station location, card count/color, marker movement, existing cubes, continued infection, and immediate eradication if no cubes remain.

answers.answer: Normally, give or take the City card matching the city both players occupy. Both players must be in that same city and agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge action: matching current-city card, both in same city, both agree; over-7 recipient immediately discards or plays an Event.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher's hand to a player in the same city, on either player's turn. The exception does not let another player give an arbitrary nonmatching card to the Researcher; transfers to the Researcher still require the matching city card under the stated exception.
answers.evidence: Researcher role: any City card may be given by the Researcher on either player's turn; it does not allow arbitrary nonmatching cards to be given to the Researcher.

answers.answer: After the actions phase, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and players lose; do not reshuffle discards. The summary does not specify a separate loss check before the draw when fewer than 2 remain; it states the loss occurs when you need to draw.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: draw top 2 together; fewer than 2 remain when needed means loss and discards are not reshuffled.

answers.answer: Resolve Increase, Infect, then Intensify. Increase the Infection Rate marker by one. For Infect, draw the bottom Infection card and place enough matching cubes to bring that city's total to 3; if it already had two, add 1, then an outbreak occurs. Discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify reshuffles only the Infection Discard Pile and places it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game and draw no replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: three ordered steps; place cubes to reach 3 and outbreak if the city already had cubes; discard the card; reshuffle only the Infection Discard Pile on top; no replacement draw.

answers.answer: After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics, respectively: 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards per turn.
answers.evidence: Player Reference, Infection Rate Track table: Epidemics Resolved 0–6 maps to 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4 cards flipped.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic through all three steps, then the second through all three steps. Events may be played between them. If the hand is over limit, resolve any drawn Epidemics first, then discard cards or play Events until at most 7 remain.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once and Hand Limit: resolve each fully in sequence; Events may be played between; resolve drawn Epidemics before reducing over-limit hand.

answers.answer: Flip cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For a non-eradicated disease, place 1 matching cube on the named city; if the city already has 3 of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. For an eradicated disease, place no cube. A cured but not eradicated disease can still receive cubes. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck, rate number one at a time; eradicated skips cube; 4th cube triggers outbreak; each card discarded. Cure Procedure says cured disease still infects until eradication.

answers.answer: An outbreak advances the Outbreaks marker, then places one cube on every connected city. A connected city already holding 3 of that color causes a chain-reaction outbreak after the current outbreak resolves, advancing the marker again. During chain reactions, do not add cubes to a city that has already had an outbreak while resolving the current Infection card, so spread does not return into the first outbreak city. Different colors can each have up to 3 cubes in a city; the cap is per color.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker moves forward; connected cities receive cubes; chain reactions follow current outbreak; no cubes added to cities that already had an outbreak during this Infection card; multiple colors up to 3 each.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played between drawing an Infection card and resolving it, so it cannot move the Quarantine Specialist before that outbreak. It may be played after that card is resolved and before the next card is drawn. The Event player's choice determines its use; it costs no action, and the played Event goes to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any player may play Events at any time, not an action; cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card; player who plays chooses use; played Events go to Player Discard Pile.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. The limit is 1 stored card, and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Contingency Planner role: action, Event from anywhere in Player Discard Pile, storage limit 1, not in hand limit, remove from game when played.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own. Moving another player's pawn requires its owner's agreement. Direct/Charter Flight discards come from the Dispatcher's hand; for Charter Flight the card matches the moved pawn's departure city. The Dispatcher may move another pawn but cannot make it Treat Disease or take another nonmovement action, and cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Dispatcher role: both movement options and agreement requirement; flight discards from Dispatcher hand; Charter card matches moved pawn departure; no treating/nonmovement; no Operations Expert move.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. The three losses are: the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak), the required disease cubes cannot be placed because the supply is exhausted (during an Epidemic, outbreak, or infection), or a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions because fewer than 2 remain. The cube-supply loss is immediate when placement is required and impossible.
answers.evidence: Victory and Defeat: cures for all 4 win regardless of cubes; three loss conditions; cube-supply check says immediate loss if needed cubes cannot be placed.

answers.answer: Place the board within reach; put the 6 research stations and disease cubes nearby; place one research station in Atlanta; put the Outbreaks marker on 0 and the four cure markers vial-side up by the Cure Indicators. Give each player a Reference card; shuffle Role cards and deal one face up to each; put matching pawns in Atlanta; remove unused Role cards and pawns. The first player is the one with the highest-population City card. The summary also says to set aside any supplied research stations beyond six.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 1–5 and 9, plus edge case: board/supplies, Atlanta station, markers, role/reference distribution and unused pieces, highest-population City card, extras set aside.

answers.answer: Teammates may offer advice, but the active player decides what to do. In Introductory games, play with cards face up for all to see. In Standard/Heroic, hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may examine either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Special Rules: active player decides; introductory hands face up; Standard/Heroic private by default with optional open hands; anyone may examine either discard pile.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube before a disease is cured has no effect; it is not eradicated. If the last cube of a cured disease is removed, it is eradicated and its cure marker is flipped to the eradication side. Thereafter, normal infections and Epidemics place no new cubes of that disease.
answers.evidence: Eradication: last cube of cured disease triggers eradication and marker flip; last cube of uncured disease has no effect; eradicated diseases receive no new cubes during infections or epidemics.

answers.answer: Place 3 cubes in the unprotected city because it has zero cubes of that color. Reaching exactly 3 does not itself cause an outbreak; an outbreak occurs if the city already has 3 and a further cube is required. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify reshuffles that pile onto the top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Infect step: place 3 cubes; only if the city already has cubes add enough to reach 3, then outbreak; discard card before Intensify.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. No cubes are placed for an eradicated disease. The drawn Infection card is still discarded to the Infection Discard Pile, and Intensify still reshuffles only that pile onto the top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic steps list Increase and Intensify; Infect places cubes ‘unless eradicated’; card is discarded. Eradicated diseases receive no new cubes.

answers.answer: The first Intensify empties the Infection Discard Pile. The second Epidemic's bottom Infection card is therefore the only card shuffled during the second Intensify; it ends up on top. The second Epidemic has already placed 3 cubes in its city, which initially had zero, so when the next normal Infection draws that city, it causes an outbreak.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once: after first Intensify discard pile is empty; second bottom card alone is shuffled and placed on top; summary says it normally causes an outbreak, but it also states outbreak requires a city already at 3 cubes.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs only 4 City cards of the same color instead of 5. The cure must still be discovered at any research station; the station city's color need not match the disease color.
answers.evidence: Scientist role and Cure Procedure: four same-color cards; at any research station, whose city color need not match.

answers.answer: As an action, the Operations Expert builds a research station in the city the Expert currently occupies. No City card is needed, used, or discarded.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert role: as an action, build a station in the current city with no City card needed, used, or discarded.

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The summary does not say that the destination needs a station.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert role: once per turn as an action, move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.

answers.answer: The Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the Medic's city, even for an uncured disease. It does not remove multiple colors at once; each different color requires a separate action.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease base rule: remove 1 cube of a chosen color; each different color uses a separate action. Medic role changes this to all cubes of one color, not multiple colors.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered, if the Medic is already in a city with cubes of that color, remove those cubes immediately. Later, entering another city via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player's turn also triggers automatic removal of all cubes of the cured color from the Medic's city. No action is needed for either automatic removal.
answers.evidence: Medic role: immediately removes cubes in the Medic's current city when cure is discovered; entering via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player's turn triggers automatic removal; cured-color automatic removal costs no action.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the Medic's city. This does not protect adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Medic role: prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in Medic's city, but not adjacent cities or uncured diseases.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents disease cube placement and outbreaks of every color in the Specialist's current city and all connected cities. The ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Quarantine Specialist role: all disease colors, current and connected cities; setup cubes are unaffected.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any 1 card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between the Infect and Intensify steps of an Epidemic, so it can remove the Infection card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify shuffles the remaining discard pile.
answers.evidence: Resilient Population: remove any 1 card in Infection Discard Pile from game; may be played between Epidemic Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, so no Infection cards are flipped for that step. It does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event Cards table, One Quiet Night: skip next Infect Cities step and do not flip cards; does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any one pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event Cards table, Airlift: move any 1 pawn to any city; permission for another player's pawn.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card limit. Role and Reference cards do not count, and the Contingency Planner's stored Event does not count. The summary says to reduce an over-limit hand by discarding cards or playing Event cards until at most 7 remain; it does not prescribe a different priority between those two choices.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only, Role and Reference cards excluded; Contingency Planner storage excluded in role rule; over-limit hand reduced by discarding or playing Events.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, regardless of the player's location, with no card discard needed.
answers.evidence: Event Cards table, Government Grant: place a research station in any city with no card discard needed.

answers.answer: Forecast lets the player draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put them back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards table, Forecast: top 6 Infection Deck cards are drawn, viewed, rearranged, and put back on top.
